newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Handelsbanken sees Sweden govt rejecting early EMU.
newsitem.headline: Handelsbanken sees Sweden govt rejecting early EMU.

text.p: Sweden's Handelsbanken said on Monday that the Swedish government would probably reject joining the first round of the European economic and monetary union (EMU) next month.
"The government on the EMU question will probably in March say that Sweden will not join in 1999," the bank said in an economic forecast.
Handelsbanken said it expected that EMU would be a big issue ahead of Sweden's general election in September 1998.
The bank said it was unclear if Sweden later this year would keep the option open to join EMU in the next phase in 2001.
"The government can take a position in the spring of 1998 on whether Sweden should join EMU in the second round or not," the bank said.
Handelsbanken said the reasons were increasing for the government to take a positive attitude towards ERM2 if the international interest rate situation got worse next year.

"If the parliament does not make the necessary constitutional changes in 1997, and if the international rate situation gets worse in 1998, this increases the reasons for the government to take a positive stand on ERM2," the bank said.
